annotations.text:
Five directions, same turn on The Fridge — sloper + crux + smear edge, Open Hand / Lock Off / Smear in hand, pump 7 of 11.
Same content everywhere so the STYLE is the only variable.

A · FIELD GUIDE — what ships today, tightened.
A guidebook you are annotating: ruled cream paper, oxide red, Georgia. Exact shipping values (#e8e1d0 / #26221e / #8c3124, stone wall vs paper hand, tan margin stripe).
Trade: warmest and most literate; also the quietest — low contrast outdoors, reads more book than game.

B · TOPO DARK — the route as a technical drawing.
Night slate, contour header with the crux ringed, monospace figures, cyan/amber channel. Bite and Grip become big readable numerals.
Trade: best legibility of the five and a real night mode; colder — an instrument, not a story.

C · CHALK & SLATE — the material the sport is made of.
Rock ground, chalk-white condensed caps (Oswald), your hand printed as chalk blocks on dark stone. Highest contrast between wall and hand.
Trade: the most physical and the most striking; heavy, and 9px serif detail is working hard on a phone.

D · EXPEDITION ARCHIVE — leans hardest into the fiction.
Halloway's field book: manila, typewriter, tape, a rotated ACT II stamp, oxblood rules. The screen becomes a page of the dead man's records.
Trade: most characterful and most on-theme for The Lost Line; busiest, and the texture fights a fast turn loop.

E · GRANITE — the store-screenshot direction.
Stone greys, one safety-orange accent, Space Grotesk, soft tiles, 44px+ targets. Cleanest and most modern; scales to tablet without redrawing.
Trade: legible and familiar — and it could be any app. Loses the handmade character the game has now.
